subject: economics
question_text: In situations with high risks, credit might create further problems for the borrower. Explain.
answer_text: In situations with high risks, credit might create further problems for the borrower. This is also known as a debt-trap. Taking credit involves an interest rate on the loan and if this is not paid back, then the borrower is forced to give up his collateral or asset used as the guarantee, to the lender. Thus, in situations with high risks, if the risks affect a borrower badly, then he ends up losing more than he would have without the loan.
final_answer: Therefore, high-risk situations can lead to borrowers losing more than they would without taking a loan.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of credit risks and their implications.

subject: economics
question_text: How does money solve the problem of double coincidence of wants? Explain with an example of your own.
answer_text: Money solves the problem of double coincidence of wants by acting as a medium of exchange. Double coincidence of wants implies a situation where two parties agree to sell and buy each other's commodities. Money does away with this tedious and complex situation by acting as a medium of exchange that can be used for one and all commodities. For example, if an ice-cream vendor wants a bicycle but the bicycle manufacturer wants clothes, and not ice-creams, then the vendor can use money to obtain a bicycle. He does need to adhere to the bicycle man's needs because money acts as the common medium of exchange. Similarly, the bicycle manufacturer can then use the money to buy clothes.
final_answer: Thus, money facilitates transactions by eliminating the need for a double coincidence of wants.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding the concept of money and its role in trade.

subject: economics
question_text: Look at a 10 rupee note. What is written on top? Can you explain this statement?
answer_text: A ten rupee note has 'Reserve Bank of India' written at the top, along with a statement 'guaranteed by the central government', following it. It is a promissory note and can only be issued by the Reserve Bank of India which supervises all money-related functions in the formal sector, in India. The statement on the ten rupee bank note relates to this idea that the RBI is the central organ in the working of money-related activities.
final_answer: Thus, the note signifies the authority of the RBI in issuing currency.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires basic understanding of currency and its issuing authority.

subject: economics
question_text: Why do we need to expand formal sources of credit in India?
answer_text: We need to expand formal sources of credit in India for two main reasons. Firstly, to reduce dependence on informal sources of credit because the latter charge high interest rates and do not benefit the borrower much. Secondly, they will be able to provide loans to a larger group of people who trust government sanctioning more than a private loaning system.
final_answer: Therefore, expanding formal credit sources can enhance financial inclusion and reduce exploitation.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding the implications of credit sources on borrowers.

subject: economics
question_text: What is the basic idea behind the SHGs for the poor? Explain in your own words.
answer_text: The basic idea behind the SHGs for the poor is to provide them with a vista for self-help in financial areas. A self-help group is a small group comprising people in the rural areas who collect their savings, and loan these out to members on an interest rate lower than that charged by the informal sector. If the SHG functions well for over a year, then it becomes eligible for loans from banks. Such loans are then used for creating self-employment opportunities for the poor. Thus, they become economically upgraded, and are not dependent on moneylenders anymore.
final_answer: Thus, SHGs empower the poor by providing them with financial resources and independence.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of SHGs and their impact on poverty alleviation.

subject: economics
question_text: What are the reasons why the banks might not be willing to lend to certain borrowers?
answer_text: Banks might not be willing to lend to people who cannot provide collateral, who do not have steady earnings or jobs, and who have a history of non-repayment of loans. In such cases, banks do not have a guarantee as to whether or not the loans will be repaid by the persons concerned. It has to be understood that banks only mediate between those who have surplus money and those who need money. Banks in fact borrow the money deposited with them, and lend it out to persons requiring money. They would thus be unwilling to advance the money to individuals from whom repayment is uncertain.
final_answer: Therefore, banks assess risk before lending to ensure loan repayment.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding banking policies and borrower assessment.

subject: economics
question_text: Analyse the role of credit for development.
answer_text: Credit plays a crucial role in a country's development. By sanctioning loans to developing industries and trade, banks provide them with the necessary aid for improvement. This leads to increased production, employment and profits. However, caution must be exercised in the case of high risks so that losses do not occur. This advantage of loans also needs to be manipulated and kept under an administrative hold because loans from the informal sector include high interest rates that may be more harmful than good. For this reason, it is important that the formal sector gives out more loans so that borrowers are not duped by moneylenders, and can ultimately contribute to national development.
final_answer: Thus, credit is essential for economic growth and development.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the role of credit in economic development.

subject: economics
question_text: Manav needs a loan to set up a small business. On what basis will Manav decide whether to borrow from the bank or the moneylender? Discuss.
answer_text: Manav will decide on whether to borrow from the bank or the moneylender on the basis of various factors. Firstly, he must have a collateral or asset which can guarantee his loan. If he lacks such an asset, Manav cannot get a loan from a bank. In this scenario, he will have to go to a moneylender, even though the latter charges a higher interest rate. Secondly, if Manav is not aware of the banes of borrowing from the informal sector, he might not even consider taking a bank loan. Thirdly, if there are no banks in or near his area of residence or work, then Manav will borrow from a moneylender.
final_answer: Therefore, Manav's decision will depend on his collateral, awareness of loan terms, and availability of banks.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding various factors influencing loan decisions.

subject: economics
question_text: In India, about 80 per cent of farmers are small farmers, who need credit for cultivation. (a) Why might banks be unwilling to lend to small farmers? (b) What are the other sources from which the small farmers can borrow? (c) Explain with an example how the terms of credit can be unfavourable for the small farmer. (d) Suggest some ways by which small farmers can get cheap credit.

mcq_options.option_text: Why might banks be unwilling to lend to small farmers?
What are the other sources from which the small farmers can borrow?
Explain with an example how the terms of credit can be unfavourable for the small farmer.
Suggest some ways by which small farmers can get cheap credit.

parts.part_text: Why might banks be unwilling to lend to small farmers?
parts.answer_text: Banks might be unwilling to lend to small farmers for lack of a collateral or asset on the part of the farmers.
parts.final_answer: Thus, lack of collateral is a major reason for banks' reluctance.

parts.part_text: What are the other sources from which the small farmers can borrow?
parts.answer_text: The other sources from which the small farmers can borrow are moneylenders, relatives or friends, self-help groups and cooperative banks.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, small farmers have multiple borrowing options.

parts.part_text: Explain with an example how the terms of credit can be unfavourable for the small farmer.
parts.answer_text: The terms of credit can be unfavourable for the small farmer if he has a bad crop, and is forced to either surrender his collateral (if he borrowed from a bank) or sell off a part of his land (if he borrowed from the informal sector), in order to repay his loan.
parts.final_answer: Thus, adverse crop conditions can lead to severe financial consequences for small farmers.

parts.part_text: Suggest some ways by which small farmers can get cheap credit.
parts.answer_text: Self-help groups and cooperative banks do not require a collateral as a guarantee; hence, they can provide cheap credit to the small farmers.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, these institutions can help small farmers access affordable credit.

difficulty_reasoning: Involves multiple aspects of credit access and its implications for small farmers.

subject: economics
question_text: Fill in the blanks: (i) Majority of the credit needs of the __________ households are met from informal sources. (ii) __________ costs of borrowing increase the debt-burden. (iii) __________ issues currency notes on behalf of the Central Government. (iv) Banks charge a higher interest rate on loans than what they offer on __________. (v) __________ is an asset that the borrower owns and uses as a guarantee until the loan is repaid to the lender.
answer_text: (i) Majority of the credit needs of the poor households are met from informal sources. (ii) High costs of borrowing increase the debt-burden. (iii) Reserve Bank of India issues currency notes on behalf of the Central Government. (iv) Banks charge a higher interest rate on loans than what they offer on deposits. (v) Collateral is an asset that the borrower owns and uses as a guarantee until the loan is repaid to the lender.
final_answer: Thus, these fill-in-the-blank statements highlight key concepts in credit and banking.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires recall of basic concepts related to credit and banking.
